newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Greece receives Russian gas supplies via Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Greece receives Russian gas supplies via Bulgaria.

text.p: Bulgarian gas monopoly Bulgargas said on Wednesday that Greece had started receiving its first supplies of Russian natural gas via Bulgaria.
A Bulgargas statement said a batch of gas transiting the Bulgarian-Greek border checkpoint at Kulata had arrived on Tuesday.
The first supplies of Russian gas to Greece are expected to total 500,000 cubic metres via a 70-km transit pipeline, reaching 60 million cubic metres by year-end, the statement said.
More than one billion cubic metres of gas will be supplied to Greece in 1997, it added.
Greece's Public Gas Corporation SA (DEPA) will start distributing gas to its industrial consumers in Athens first and later in Thessaloniki, Bulgargas officials said.
DEPA's general manager Spiros Paleoyannis has said gas supplies to Greece will be increased to 2.4 billion cubic metres per year by 2002.
In addition to Greece, Bulgaria supplies Russian gas to Turkey.

Bulgaria's transit gas network totalling some 2,000 km also has a link with Macedonia, which is filled with gas. But Sofia is waiting for Macedonia to complete construction of the pipeline on their territory.
A new link with Serbia is also being planned.
